jurisdiction.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines has published no national AI law, strategy, guidance or regulator AI document. Its data protection law, the Privacy Act 2003, is not confirmed to be in force, and a national digital economy transformation strategy funded under the World Bank's Caribbean Digital Transformation Project has not yet been published.
lead_institutions: Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
narrative.review_notes: The House of Assembly's and the Ministry of Education's websites were searched on 18 October 2026 alongside the government portal, the finance ministry and the telecommunications regulator, and no AI law, bill, strategy or guidance was found; the official gazette is not searchable online. The Privacy Act 2003 and the digital economy strategy remain tracked as pending documents. Not yet verified from the official text: material from the online laws portal and the Attorney General's website, and that the Privacy Act 2003 has never been brought into force.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines' government portal, House of Assembly, ministries and regulators were searched for AI laws, strategies, policies and guidance. No qualifying AI-governance document was found in any category. The gazette cannot be searched online, so a direct search of enacted legislation for AI is still outstanding.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. laws.gov.vc, attorneygeneral.gov.vc proxy 502; assembly.gov.vc, education.gov.vc certificate mismatch; gazette not searchable online. gov.vc, NTRC, FSA site searches: nothing. Cybercrime Act 2016 PDF scanned (no text layer). Intelligent video analytics project is government use (out of scope §1). Party election manifesto AI pledge excluded (not a government document). Convention 108: not a party. Units covered: Law: Searched, nothing found: no AI law, AI provision, deepfake offence or AI bill located. gov.vc Acts, Bills and Policies page checked (Cybercrime Act 2016: general cybercrime offences law, scanned PDF without a text layer, no AI provision reported; FOI Act 2003). Privacy Act 2003 reported not in force and its official text not found (lead). Dedicated legislation/House of Assembly/Attorney General hosts unreachable (proxy 502 / certificate mismatch).; Government: Searched, nothing found: no national AI strategy, AI policy, public-sector AI guideline or AI governance framework on gov.vc (site search for AI, generative, ChatGPT, machine learning returned no relevant item). National digital economy transformation strategy under CARDTP commissioned but unpublished (lead). A 2025 party manifesto AI pledge is a party document, not a government one.; Ministries: Searched, nothing found: Education (gov.vc releases on digital transformation in classrooms and regional education meetings, no AI guidance; education.gov.vc unreachable), Finance/Economic Planning/IT (CARDTP items, no AI document), National Security/Police (video analytics project, no instrument; lead), Health, Justice, Labour: no AI documents on gov.vc.; Regulators: Searched, nothing found: NTRC (site search, no AI document), Financial Services Authority (site search, no AI document); no data protection authority exists (Privacy Act 2003 not in force); no national cyber security agency or standards body AI material found. ECCB/ECTEL are regional bodies (not national records).. Not reached: Official legislation portal / House of Assembly / Attorney General's Chambers sites (laws.gov.vc, assembly.gov.vc, attorneygeneral.gov.vc unreachable: proxy 502 or certificate mismatch); Official Gazette not searchable online; Ministry of Education own site (education.gov.vc certificate mismatch). Could not verify: Official legislation portal / House of Assembly / Attorney General sites unreachable, so a gazette search for 'artificial intelligence' could not be run directly; the absence finding for Law relies on gov.vc and web discovery. binding-law, strategy, government-governance, ethics, risk-assurance, public-sector, procurement, cyber-security, data-privacy, transparency, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, sectoral, generative-ai, drafts, international, historical: no material found. leads.title: Privacy Act, 2003
leads.issuing_authority: Parliament (House of Assembly) of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
leads.note: General data protection law covering public authorities' handling of personal data; reported as enacted but not brought into force (no commencement order located). No official full text found on gov.vc (its Acts, Bills and Policies page lists only the Freedom of Information Act 2003, Cybercrime Act 2016 and a 2018 bill); legislation portal hosts (laws/assembly/attorney-general gov.vc) unreachable. Contains no known AI-specific provision; record under data-privacy only if the official text and commencement are confirmed. 2026-10-18: House of Assembly site now reachable; its Acts, Bills and Policies page and site search (privacy, data protection) show no Privacy Act 2003 text and no data protection bill. Laws portal and Attorney General's site still unreachable. Remains a lead.

leads.title: National Digital Economy Transformation Strategy (Caribbean Digital Transformation Project, CARDTP)
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Finance, Economic Planning and Information Technology (Caribbean Digital Transformation Project unit)
leads.note: Five-year national digital economy strategy commissioned under the World Bank-financed CARDTP (contract award notice on gov.vc; visioning workshop gov.vc media-center item 3020). No published strategy text found as of 2026-10-12; check for an AI pillar once published. 2026-10-18: still no published strategy text found on gov.vc or finance.gov.vc.

leads.title: Enhancing Public Safety With Intelligent Video Analytics Project
leads.english_title: Enhancing Public Safety With Intelligent Video Analytics Project
leads.issuing_authority: Information Technology Services Division (ITSD) / Royal Saint Vincent and the Grenadines Police Force, with the Republic of China (Taiwan)
leads.note: Government deployment of CCTV with video analytics and licence-plate recognition (second phase launched 29 September 2023, gov.vc media-center item 3279). Institutional use of AI-type technology with no governing instrument (no rules, policy or guidance published); out of scope under PROTOCOL §1, kept as context. 2026-10-18: no governing instrument found; unchanged.
